# Step 2.69: tracker clock switch, mercy and the last-minutes sign

## Builder one: layer 1 (the tracker's parts and their component tests)

What exists:

- `apps/web/src/features/tracker/clock-mode.ts`: what the screen shows of the clock mode, read only from the engine (`clockModeAt`, `inLastMinutes`, a basket's `mercyClock`): the mode in force, whether the last-minutes stop clock holds, when it begins, what the switch sends, and the mercy rule's switch while it still holds. `packages/sports` is unchanged: the engine already knew every rule.
- The running-clock switch (`role="switch"`, `data-clock-switch`) in the clock's form, beside its title, so it takes no height; it sends the `clock-mode` command through the controller like any tap (queued with no signal, shown as unsaved, replayed with the same id).
- The mercy notice (`MercyNotice`, `data-mercy-notice`) in the screen's notices: "Stop the clock on fouls again" sends `clock-mode` stop, "Keep it running" hides it for that basket.
- The sign: "Stop clock" beside the period on the scoreboard (`data-last-minutes`), with a full sentence for a screen reader; the screen draws itself again as the window begins while the clock runs.
- Words in `packages/site/src/messages/en/tracker.ts` (`tracker.clock.lastMinutes*`, `tracker.clockMode.*`, `tracker.mercy.*`). Decisions: `S-112` (decided for you), `T-410`; P7 section 5.2 says where the switch is.

Run and passed: `clock-mode.test.ts` (7 tests); the tracker and site folders (887 tests); `npm run check`; `npm run typecheck`; the browser test `scoring-screen-test`. Its first run failed: the switch as its own row of the clock's form did not fit 390 x 664 or 844 x 390, and sat 6 apart from the period buttons; moved beside the title, it passes.

Broken by hand once each, and the test failed: the switch always sending running; the mercy notice not ending at a switch by hand (it first passed, so a case was added); the sign shown while the scorer kept a running clock in the last minutes; the sign's mark removed from the clock button. The offline replay test is of the controller, which needed no change, so it was not broken by hand.

What is left (layer 2):

- A browser test that plays a mercy-rule game end to end (the made-up league's season needs a mercy lead and a last-minutes window for it), through the switch, the notice and the sign.
- Page-step checks, and the pinned lists of brief-common rule 9 for that test; no page, route, command or read was added here.
- Pictures at the five sizes: `scripts/tracker-shots.mjs --chapter=clock` stopped at state 09 (a turnover button not found), before any of this step's states; not looked into.

What I distrust:

- The mercy notice and the "Stop clock" word were not seen at the five sizes: the browser test reaches neither. On an upright phone the notice is drawn in the pad at rest.
- The dismissal is kept only while the screen is open: after a reload the notice is said again for the same basket.
- The switch beside the title was measured by the browser test only in this computer's letters and the wider face it uses.

## Builder two: layer 2 (the browser test, the pictures, the pinned lists)

What exists:

- `tests/browser/mercy-rule-test.mjs` (builds the app itself): the owner gives the season a stop clock with a mercy lead of 10; 11–0 crosses it, the notice says so and "Stop the clock on fouls again" stops the clock; 13–3 crosses again and "Keep it running" hides it; a reload does not bring it back; with no signal the switch is turned off (shown "waiting", sent as one command once the signal returns), then on again; the game is ended and the public page says 3–13 final. The season cannot hold a mercy lead and a last-minutes stop clock together, so the "Stop clock" sign is played in a second game (Lions at Hawks) after the season is given a running clock stopping in the last 2 minutes: no sign at 2:10, drawn as the running clock reaches 2:00 (T-412).
- The lead's decision: a dismissed mercy notice is kept in the device's storage by game and person (`clock-mode.ts`, `readMercyDismissed`/`writeMercyDismissed`), read by the scoring screen as the Players panel reads its drafts (T-411; T-410's wording and P7 section 5.2 corrected).
- `seasonClock` in `tests/browser/tracker-driver.mjs` (the season's clock in "Game rules", as its owner sets it).
- `scripts/tracker-shots.mjs`: every world's season keeps turnovers first, so `--chapter=clock` runs to state 40 again; new chapters `mercy` (63 the switch, 64 the notice) and `last-minutes` (65 the sign), at phone-upright and phone-lying only.
- Seen at 390 x 844 and 844 x 390: the sign fits both; the notice lying down fits. Upright, "Keep it running" fell below the pad's foot: in the pad the two answers now share one row (`court.css`, `.court-notices-pad .court-mercy-acts`), seen again and fitting.

Run and passed: `clock-mode.test.ts` (8 tests); `mercy-rule-test` (14 checks); `tracker-shots.mjs --chapter=clock`, `mercy`, `last-minutes`. Broken by hand once each and failed: the dismissal not written (the component test); the dismissal not read at opening (the browser test, "after a reload the dismissed notice stays away").

Pinned lists: none applies. No page, route, field, message, command or read was added; the new browser test is only a file; `tracker-driver.mjs` was already a helper.

Lines in other lanes' folders: none.

What I distrust:

- The spec (P7 section 5.2, S-28 to S-32: "inside them the stop clock wins over the mercy rule") speaks of the mercy rule and the last-minutes stop clock meeting, but `packages/contracts/src/season-rules.ts` refuses a season with both. One of them is wrong; a product question for the lead, not changed here.
- The notice was not seen at 390 x 664 (the phone in its browser) nor at the tablet sizes; the one-row answers in the pad wrap to two lines there.
- The offline switch is checked by the commands the page sent; it does not prove the server kept no second copy beyond the replay having one id.

## Review

Used in a browser by a throwaway script (the lane's `.local/review-269.mjs`, not committed) at 390 x 664, 844 x 390 and a tablet 820 x 1180; three pictures looked at.

- **Medium**, `clock-parts.tsx` `MercyNotice` in the pad (`scoring-screen.tsx` 1569–1588, `court.css` `.court-notices-pad`): at 390 x 664 the notice appears in the pad exactly where the scorer's finger just was. The "+2" tapped for #9 was at y 543–599; the notice's two answers appear at y 587–647, under the lower 12 px of it, both answers. A quick second tap (a double tap, or the next basket of the same player) lands on "Stop the clock on fouls again" or "Keep it running". Seen by measuring the tap's box before and the notice's buttons after. A short rest (as Undo and Start already have, `data-resting`) on the notice's answers would stop it.
- **Medium**, `court.css` 800 (`.court-notices`, the top place used at 844 x 390 and on a tablet): the notice is a row of its own above the courts, so the basket that crosses the line moves every player tile, the pad and Undo down by about 90 px (844 x 390: notice y 56–146, courts from y 152). A tap meant for the next player lands a row off. The same was true of the earlier notices; this is the first one a basket brings up mid-play.
- **Low (latent)**, `clock-mode.ts` 66–75 and `scoring-screen.tsx` 1578: `mercySwitch` shows the notice whenever the derived mode is running, and "back" always sends `stop`. Inside a last-minutes window the mode in force is already `stop` (`clockModeAt`), so the notice would claim the clock "keeps running" and "back" would be refused by the engine ("must change"). Not reachable today because the contract refuses the pair (below); it must be fixed before the pair is allowed.
- **Low**, `clock-mode.ts` 85: one storage key per game and person, never removed, so a scorekeeper's phone gains one key per game scored. Small, but endless; keeping only the latest few games, or one key holding a short map, would bound it.
- **Low**, `mercy-rule-test.mjs` 180–189: "a new device sees the switch kept once" checks only that the mode reads running, not that one `clock-mode` play was kept. A second scoring device is taken over ("Someone else is now scoring this game"), and no read-only page shows the clock mode, so "a second device watching" has nothing to show today.
- **Low (engine, not this step)**: inside the window, Off then On by hand (`running` with `lastMinutes`, then `stop`) leaves the whole game on a stop clock after the window ends, and the sign goes while the stop clock holds; the switch does read Off, so the scorer sees it.

Attacks that held: undo of the crossing basket puts the stop clock back and hides the notice, redo brings both back; after "Stop the clock on fouls again" a lead growing 11 → 13 does not switch again; falling under and crossing again (16–6) is a new notice; the switch tapped twice fast is sent once (the form closes on the first tap, the second lands on the page title); with storage refused (a private window, `localStorage` throwing) the page opens and "Keep it running" still hides the notice, no page errors; the key holds the account and the game. By reading: the sign is right at a period change (a `period` play ends the window's override), in every overtime period (`inLastMinutes`) and when the clock is set by hand into the window (the screen is drawn again with the new time).

The spec and the code: the engine already handles a mercy lead and a last-minutes stop clock together with the stop clock winning (`clockModeAt`, `packages/sports/src/basketball/live.ts` 185–200; `tests/live-stats-mercy.test.mjs` 123, step 2.67, 2026-11-14). The contract's refusal is older: `packages/contracts/src/season-rules.ts` 126–131 and 138–140 came with the season rules document (step 2.5, 2026-11-13), keyed on the clock the game starts with. To allow both: let `stopClockLastSeconds` stand beside a stop clock with a mercy lead (and its test in `season-rules.test.ts`), show that field in the season's game rules form, check `season-rules-reach-engine.test.ts`, and fix the latent notice fault above. A product question for the lead, nothing changed here.

Tests read: no check passes on a timeout or behind a `.catch`, every wait is bounded (Playwright's 30 s default at least); the existing unit tests only gained the new `mode` field and `switchClock`; `scoring-screen-test` and `scoring-plays-test` are unchanged. Broken by hand once: the dismissal key without the account (`mercyDismissedKey`); `clock-mode.test.ts` failed (1 of 8), restored.
